To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important features of Auger showers, such as the muon content, can be reproduced by the standard scenario, but that a more realistic treatment of hadronic interactions is needed to fully understand the shower development and the observed features.

the most relevant observabilities are: (i) the average number of particles, (ii) the average number per shower of particles with energies above 1 GeV, (iii) the average total energy of the shower, (iv) the average number in the core of particles with energies larger than 1 GeV and (v) the depth of shower maximum.

the most important effects are: (a) an enhancement of the muon flux, (b) an enhancement of muon lateral distribution at the ground, (c) a suppression of the electron flux, (d) an increase of the electron lateral distribution, (e) a decrease of the shower maximum.
